result.reason: All 9 immutable criteria MET, each independently reproduced rather than read. RUNTIME SMOKE nobody had run: the plist invokes /bin/bash healthcheck.sh whose `python3` resolves under launchd's minimal PATH to /usr/bin/python3 **3.9.6** (venv is 3.14) — seam executes correctly there (`true stale_401_ignored_...`, exit 0), safe only because `from __future__ import annotations` covers the `tuple[str,str]` hints. INDEPENDENT MUTATION MATRIX (mine, 9 mutants on a scratchpad copy tree, repo never written; control + restore both 13 passed): 7 KILLED. MQ-1 (criterion 7's exact mutation, `fresh = True`) reproduced the required pattern precisely — `3 failed, 10 passed` with test_c3_stale_401 and test_c4_regression RED and test_c3_fresh_401 GREEN. Fixture-side mutants MQ-F1 (drop os.utime) and MQ-F3 (401 payload carrying no 401) both KILLED, so the fixtures are load-bearing, not pseudo-tests. Two survivors, both characterized as NON-findings by executed differentials: MQ-6 (fail-open→raise on the session read) yields ok→`unknown probe_error` at exit 0, never `false`, so criterion 6's no-manufactured-P1 guarantee holds in both arms; MQ-F2 (drop the `_run` returncode assert) is equivalent under the current seam. All three cycle-1 findings genuinely closed, each proven by execution not by reading the claim: (1) BLOCK lint — `sys` gone, gate clean over the derived scope; (2) WARN DD-5 — my MQ-2 (guard relaxed to `if auth_ok == "false"`) is KILLED by the new test_c5_dd5_apply_transition_guard_driven_directly; (3) WARN drill isolation — verified BEHAVIOURALLY by evaluating healthcheck.sh's exact lines 105-106 in real bash with a shadowing stub: normal run passes `--apply` (APPLIED), drill run withholds it (WITHHELD), so the 62.5 contract holds by construction, not by comment. MQ-C also closed (my MQ-3 KILLED by test_after_clear_suppresses_repage_for_pre_clear_401). LIVE CLAIMS ALL RE-DERIVED BY ME AND EXACT: 474 consecutive ok:false over 9.87 days (2026-07-28T17:09:48Z..2026-08-07T14:05:18Z), auth the sole failing leg in all 474 (0 records with a non-auth failing leg), 34 ok:true of 510 pre-fix parseable, 1 unparseable line (DD-2); the criterion-8 record is present byte-for-byte (grep -cF = 1). CRITERION 8 CLOSED ON BOTH PATHS: during this evaluation the naturally-scheduled 30-min tick fired (pid 18126) and appended `2026-08-07T14:35:20Z ok=true auth_ok=true detail=ok`, and `launchctl list` flipped away-watchdog's last-exit-status from **1 to 0** — the live_check's prediction verified in-flight by me, not by the author. Criterion 9 satisfied: cause recorded AND 85.3.1 filed (P1) with its id in all three artifacts; 85.3.2/85.3.3 also queued with executor-ready scope. Harness compliance clean: research gate (7 sources read in full ≥5, 34 URLs ≥10, recency scan true, gate_passed true) precedes the contract by mtime; log-last honoured (no harness_log entry for 85.3, masterplan still `pending`); NOT verdict-shopping — the evidence materially CHANGED between cycles (11→13 tests, F401 removed, APPLY_FLAG drill gate added, the clear relocated into the seam), all verified by diff and execution, so the improved verdict is the documented cycle-2 flow, not sycophancy under rebuttal.
result.notes:
Verdict #2 for 85.3 (prior CONDITIONAL wf_9bdd4eb6-03d); harness_log carries 0 result=CONDITIONAL entries for this step-id, so the 3rd-CONDITIONAL rule is not engaged — and PASS is returned on merit, not to avoid it. Four NOTE-level findings, none criterion-violating, each with a named fix; recorded so the next cycle can tidy them:

N1 (NOTE, transcription hygiene) — experiment_results_85.3.md's block headed "## Verification (verbatim, re-derived after the final edit)" still shows `11 passed` over 11 progress dots. That is the CYCLE-1 suite; the current tree yields `13 passed`. The block is internally consistent (11 dots / 11 passed), so it is a genuine un-regenerated capture, NOT a spliced or edited one — the §4b Invalid_Precondition shape does not apply. It is superseded 40 lines later ("Suite after cycle 2: 13 passed in 0.43s") and in live_check line 63. FIX: re-run and paste, or label the block "cycle 1".

N2 (NOTE, same class) — criterion 7's "its verbatim output shape: `3 failed, 8 passed`" re-derives as `3 failed, 10 passed`. Cross-suite arithmetic proves stale transcription rather than an untested change: 3+8=11 (cycle-1 suite) vs 3+10=13 (current), the delta being exactly the two cycle-2 tests. The load-bearing content — WHICH tests go red vs green, which is all criterion 7 actually constrains — is byte-correct and I reproduced it independently under my own MQ-1. FIX: restate as `3 failed, 10 passed`.

N3 (NOTE, protocol form) — contract_85.3.md does NOT copy the 9 criteria verbatim; it compresses them to C1-C9 one-liners under a heading reading "all 9 copied verbatim into the step record" and points at masterplan.json with a read-date. CLAUDE.md's five-file protocol asks for the criteria verbatim IN the contract. No erosion actually occurred — I verified the criteria byte-identical to HEAD and evaluated all 9 against masterplan.json directly, and every C1-C9 summary is faithful. FIX: paste the criteria verbatim in the next contract.

N4 (RETIRED during evaluation) — live_check line 65's heading "Naturally-scheduled tick evidence" was ahead of its evidence at write time: both post-fix records (14:09:24Z, 14:09:40Z) were hand-runs, and the spawn prompt's framing that health.jsonl "keeps gaining ok:true records from the real scheduled watchdog" did NOT reproduce when I first checked (exactly 2 records, both manual). The artifact itself was honest about this at line 53 (disclosing launchctl still at 1 and predicting the ≈14:35Z flip). I then observed the scheduled tick land at 14:35:20Z with ok:true and launchctl flip 1→0, so the claim is now true and independently confirmed. Note for future cycles: my first read of `stat` mtimes was LOCAL CEST (16:0x) against UTC record timestamps (14:0x), which briefly looked like a 2-hour scheduling outage — I checked `date -u` before asserting, and the 30.1-min cadence was intact throughout.

Additional evaluator-side result worth carrying forward: I attempted to file the source-scan half of test_seam_reads_only_the_given_paths as a vacuity finding and DISPROVED it — an evasive repo-path fallback built from `os.path.join(_R, "handoff", "away" + "_ops")`, which never contains the scanned literal, still turned that test RED because its behavioural half (empty tmp ops dir must yield ("true","ok")) picked up the real 27-day-old 401. The scan is redundant defence-in-depth, not sole coverage. Two lessons banked to .claude/agent-memory/qa/ (production-interpreter smoke; evade-before-filing-vacuity).

Scope/authority notes: I was READ-ONLY on the repo — all mutations ran against a scratchpad copy tree (`scratchpad/mut<ts>/{scripts,backend}`) whose parents[2] resolution makes the test target my copy; control and restore both reproduced 13 passed, and I re-verified the repo seam still carries `fresh = age_s <= window_s`, `after_clear = cleared_at is None or mt > cleared_at`, and `if auth_ok != "true":` with git status showing only the 4 intended paths. I did NOT run healthcheck.sh myself (it appends to live health.jsonl and can page); the drill-isolation test evaluated only its extracted lines 105-106 with a shadowing stub. No UI claims in this step, so §1c does not apply. `set -e` is absent from healthcheck.sh, so the new `APPLY_FLAG=... && APPLY_FLAG=""` compound returning exit 1 in normal mode cannot abort the script — checked, because under `set -e` it would have. masterplan.json also gained 85.2.1/85.2.2 from the sibling 85.2 cycle; experiment_results' "+3 pending steps" claim is correct for 85.3's own additions.
